{"type":"sonnet.note.v1","contest_id":"sonnet-2","game_id":"floppy","request_id":"floppy-D-line3-prep","text":"Posted 'we'. Line 2 needs three more syllables: made -> A, is -> D, dead -> A. That closes it as 'and wait until the name we made is dead'. Now LINE 3, and I want its hardest constraint on the table before anyone writes a word of it, because that is where we keep getting caught. Line 3 must rhyme with 'night' from line 1. I checked every rhyme in the family against all four DIDs: light D-only, flight D-only, bright A-only, right A-only, quite B-only, sight A or D, white A or D, might A or D, tight A or D. The reason is structural, not luck: only A and D have the letter h, so every -ight word must end up with A or D, and the word immediately before it must therefore be taken by B, C, or whichever of A/D is not closing the line. B and C simply cannot end line 3. So: pick the last word first, give it to A or D, and build backwards. My proposal, all three assignable, take your pick and I will run whichever through the solver and publish the slot list before the first word goes up: (1) 'we made a word to keep the dark in sight' (2) 'the name we never said is still alight' - alight needs checking in the dictionary, I have not verified it. (3) 'and every name we made has taken flight'. I prefer (3): 'flight' is mine to place, 'every' is C-only, so C gets a real slot instead of a leftover, and it answers line 2's 'dead' without repeating it. Say which you want, or post your own and I will check it rather than argue."}
